tagging_basis: OCR H432 numbered specification sections (lettered learning outcomes as evidence)

units.label: 1(a)(i)
units.summary: State what is meant by an acid.

units.label: 1(a)(ii)
units.summary: State what is meant by a weak acid.

units.label: 1(b)(i)
units.summary: Record burette readings from a diagram, calculate titres and the mean titre of concordant results.
units.difficulty_basis: Several steps but routine titration handling

units.label: 1(b)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the mass of citric acid in one lime from titration data, including dilution factors.

units.label: 1(c)
units.summary: Suggest and justify a method modification to keep the same titre using a four times more dilute sodium hydroxide.

units.label: 1(d)
units.summary: Write a balanced equation for the oxidation of malic acid using [O] and show the organic product.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs identification of the secondary alcohol product

units.label: 2(a)(i)
units.summary: Write the equation for strontium reacting with water.

units.label: 2(a)(ii)
units.summary: Use oxidation numbers to explain why strontium reacting with water is redox.

units.label: 2(a)(iii)
units.summary: Explain why calcium reacts more slowly with water than strontium.

units.label: 2(b)(i)
units.summary: Predict the approximate pH of the solution formed from barium oxide and water.

units.label: 2(b)(ii)
units.summary: Give the observation and barium compound formed when dilute sulfuric acid is added to barium hydroxide solution.

units.label: 3(a)(i)
units.summary: Explain in terms of collision theory why the reaction slows and stops over time.
units.difficulty_basis: Multi-point explanation of rate and reaction ending

units.label: 3(a)(ii)
units.summary: Find the rate at 50 seconds by drawing a tangent to the mass-time graph.

units.label: 3(a)(iii)
units.summary: Sketch the mass-time curve for the reaction with acid pre-heated to 40 C.
units.difficulty_basis: Applying temperature effect to a graph

units.label: 3(b)(i)
units.summary: Describe two observations showing the catalysed reaction is faster.

units.label: 3(b)(ii)
units.summary: Sketch an enthalpy profile for catalysed and uncatalysed reactions with labelled enthalpy change and activation energies.

units.label: 4(a)(i)
units.summary: Explain why the industrial conditions are used for steam reforming of methane in terms of equilibrium and rate.
units.difficulty_basis: Six mark extended response needing equilibrium and rate integration

units.label: 4(a)(ii)
units.summary: Write the Kc expression and calculate its value from equilibrium concentrations.

units.label: 4(b)
units.summary: Calculate an enthalpy change from average bond enthalpies for the reaction of ethanol with steam.
units.difficulty_basis: Standard bond enthalpy calculation with a large number of bonds

units.label: 4(c)
units.summary: State the bond angles in carbon dioxide and water and explain the difference using electron pair repulsion.

units.label: 5(a)(i)
units.summary: State the conditions for forming bromine radicals from bromine.

units.label: 5(a)(ii)
units.summary: Write the two propagation step equations for the radical substitution of butane with bromine.

units.label: 5(a)(iii)
units.summary: Suggest two reasons for the low yield of 2-bromobutane in radical substitution.

units.label: 5(b)
units.summary: Calculate and compare atom economies to explain why addition of HBr is more sustainable than substitution.

units.label: 5(c)(i)
units.summary: Calculate the mass of butan-2-ol needed to make 10.0 g of 2-bromobutane at a given percentage yield.

units.label: 5(c)(ii)
units.summary: Describe how to obtain a pure dry sample of 2-bromobutane from the refluxed mixture.
Deduce the structure of an unsaturated trans compound from composition, mass spectrum and infrared spectrum.
units.difficulty_basis: Six mark synoptic structure deduction from several data sources
